fields.v: Tasks: 32 ten-request flows (same benchmark instances for all). Configurations: 14 models in one scaffold (OpenHands). Baseline: none (cross-model comparison); for the first request, a comparison with the WebGen-Bench Bolt.diy configuration (Haiku 4.5) is mentioned without numbers. Held constant: benchmark instances, scaffold, 20-turn budget per request, functional evaluator; isolated container per flow (6 vCPUs); vendor-recommended reasoning/sampling settings. Acceptance tests: five browser-agent tests per follow-up request (3 functional, 1 integration along a DAG edge, 1 backward). Repetitions: 3 runs for 7 closed-source models, 1 for 7 open-source. Human intervention: none; no test feedback between requests. Additional: request language (5 translations, 5 models), judge robustness (3 alternative judges)

fields.v: Fable 5 (0.694) and Kimi K3 (0.684) lead, not ranked against each other (gap within run-to-run variation); GPT 5.6 Sol 0.622; weakest Qwen3.5 35B-A3B 0.162. Tier gaps (≥ 0.05) about two SDs of the noisiest models; Opus 4.8 vs Sonnet 4.6 (0.001) within noise. For every model backward > functional > integration tests (average Grade 0.58, 0.55, 0.51); accuracy of requests 8-10 falls with DAG depth and in-degree; runtime errors rise over successive requests and track Grade (Spearman ρ = −0.72 vs −0.52 for build errors); tool-call errors do not (ρ = −0.06). Fable 5 uses the fewest turns (4.7) and about 100K output tokens per trajectory but the highest cost per sample ($14.40). Alternative judges flip only 2-3 of 28 pairs, no self-preference. Only Sonnet 4.6 is insensitive to request language. No significance tests

fields.v: Yes, by the authors' account: clear differences between model tiers, stable rankings across tolerance thresholds (exact order can change) and across judges; evaluator validated against humans (87.7% exact agreement). Repeatability: 3 runs for closed-source models only (Grade SD 0.004-0.043). Limitations stated: SDs from three runs are coarse and cover run-to-run variation only, not the choice of 32 applications; open-source models run once, so gaps of about 0.01 do not establish a ranking; language and DAG analyses lack confidence intervals; one backward test per request samples rather than audits regressions; tolerance weighting and PARTIAL = 0.5 are conventions; early evaluator errors weigh more; fail-stop ranking differs markedly from Grade

Gaps: cross-request integration and sustained runtime reliability are key weaknesses of coding agents; future work on longer trajectories and closed-loop interaction where users report failures and request repairs

Possible bias not discussed: Fable 5 generated the requests and is the top-ranked agent; the default judge (Sonnet 4.6) is also an evaluated agent (addressed by the judge-robustness study).
